parsed_answer.content: In the Spring Framework, the Java-based configuration model shifts the paradigm from XML descriptors to type-safe, programmatic bean definitions. At the core of this model lies the `@Configuration` annotation, which marks a class as a source of bean definitions and instructs the Spring IoC container to process it using CGLIB-based byte-enhancement. This enhancement intercepts invocations of methods annotated with `@Bean`, ensuring that singleton semantics are strictly enforced by returning cached instances rather than invoking the method repeatedly. Complementing this, `@ComponentScan` automates the discovery of candidate components—such as those annotated with `@Component`, `@Service`, or `@Repository`—by scanning specified packages and registering their corresponding `BeanDefinition` metadata into the `BeanDefinitionRegistry`. Finally, modularity and architectural decoupling are achieved through `@Import`, which allows developers to seamlessly bring in additional `@Configuration` classes, `ImportSelector` implementations, or `ImportBeanDefinitionRegistrar` routines into the primary application context without relying on sprawling package hierarchies.

items: When `@Configuration` is processed, Spring's `ConfigurationClassPostProcessor` uses CGLIB to subclass the configuration class at runtime, overriding `@Bean` methods to check the `BeanFactory` for an existing instance before executing the factory method.

`@ComponentScan` utilizes Spring's `MetadataReader` interface powered by the ASM library to inspect class bytecode directly without loading the actual `.class` file into the JVM Classloader during the initial scanning phase.

The `@Import` annotation supports four distinct strategies: importing a raw configuration class, importing an ImportSelector for conditional logic, importing an ImportBeanDefinitionRegistrar for programmatic bean registration, and regular component importing.

Methods annotated with `@Bean` inside classes *not* annotated with `@Configuration` (termed 'lite' mode) do not undergo CGLIB enhancement, meaning cross-method calls will instantiate new objects rather than resolving references through the IoC container.

parsed_answer.content: A classic production trap occurs when developers place `@Bean` definitions inside a standard `@Component` or `@Service` class instead of a `@Configuration` class. Because Spring does not apply CGLIB byte-enhancement to standard components ('lite' mode), any inter-bean method calls within that class will execute the factory method multiple times, bypassing the singleton cache and inadvertently spawning duplicate object instances.
